The stored point is North Lincolnshire Museum in Scunthorpe, which keeps the logboat, not the place of the find. The boat was found in 1943 on the bed of the Old River Ancholme near Appleby, but neither Wikipedia, Wikidata nor the museum's page gives coordinates for the find spot, so no two sources give the site's point.

English Wikipedia gives 10.05139 S 76.61944 W (the stored point), but Spanish Wikipedia and Wikidata, which count as the same source family, give -10.063219, -76.630634, 1.8 km away and next to the village of San José de Ticra, where the MINCETUR inventory places the site. No independent source family (no OSM node, Megalithic Portal entry or register point) gives a point for the site, so it is held for the owner.

English Wikipedia gives Tell Harmal at 33°18′34″N 44°28′01″E, next to the stored point, and Wikidata's point is a coarse minute-precision value 6 km north; but no second, independent readable source printing the site's coordinates could be found (Pleiades is behind a bot challenge, the other pages copy Wikipedia), so the point is held for the owner.

Wikidata places the temple at 33.4535234, 35.7904376 (0.03 km from the stored point) and Pleiades' place record for the Ain Hersha Roman Temple agrees (33.4535, 35.7905 in its JSON), but the Pleiades page cannot be read by the quote check (bot challenge) and no other independent page prints the temple's coordinates - English Wikipedia's point (33.456389, 35.783889) is the village of Ain Harcha - so the point is held for the owner.

The sources disagree by kilometres: German Wikipedia/Wikidata give 53.33994, 69.11968 (the stored point), English Wikipedia 53.3305, 69.1865 (4.6 km east), the Megalithic Portal 53.353, 69.157 (about 3 km from either), and a regional press report puts Krasnyi Yar 1 about 10 km west of Kokshetau; no two independent sources agree on a point, so it is held for the owner.

The sources place Marayniyoq on Vega Pampa about 4 km north of Wari (-13.0606, -74.1989); the stored point lies 2 km west of Wari, Wikidata's -13.01, -74.205 is 5.6 km north of it, MINCETUR's matching point (-13.0277, -74.2036) is not in its visible text and OpenStreetMap's 'Marayniyoq' polygon sits on Wari itself, so no two independent quotable sources agree on the site's point.

The only trace of an archaeological site 'A Figa' is a one-sentence, unreferenced Corsican Wikipedia stub (co.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Figa, 'commune of Sartène') and its Wikidata item Q2819740, whose point 41.72792, 9.40181 equals the stored one and lies on the coastal hamlet of Figa in Conca (OpenStreetMap hamlet node 41.7289, 9.4023), not on a documented monument. No register, excavation report or second independent source gives the site's position, so the point is held for the owner.

Only one source family prints a point for the Treasury of Cyrene: Wikidata Q22810178 (38.482535, 22.502622, 0.13 km from the stored placeholder point). OpenStreetMap maps the building (way 145690062, 'Θησαυρός Κυρηναίων', centre about 38.48223, 22.50214), but no readable page prints that point as a coordinate pair, and ToposText, Pleiades and the Megalithic Portal have no entry for it; so no second independent quotable point exists.
